newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU postpones Helms-Burton trade case at WTO.
newsitem.headline: EU postpones Helms-Burton trade case at WTO.

text.p: European Union member states have agreed not to present a formal complaint against the U.S. Helms-Burton Act on Monday pending a final decision later this week, EU Union Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said.
"We do not plan (to put) our case to the WTO today," Brittan told a news conference after meeting with ambassadors from the 15 EU nations.

Brittan said the ambassadors would meet again on Wednesday to decide formally whether to suspend the EU's action against the Helms-Burton Act, which seeks to discourage foreign investment in Cuba, in the World Trade Organisation.

His announcement follows a tentative deal struck between the European Commission and Washington on Friday to defuse a trans-Atlantic trade row over the Helms-Burton legislation, which aims to isolate the government of Fidel Castro.
The Europeans have been threatening high-profile action at the Geneva-based WTO in retaliation to the U.S. law.

Under the deal agreed on Friday, the EU would suspend an existing WTO panel and the two sides would negotiate a common policy on properties seized by Cuba's communist government after Castro took power in 1959.

They would also work toward a global agreement on protection of expropriated property. The White House would in exchange seek to change a key provision of Helms-Burton barring executives of companies that invest in disputed properties in Cuba from entering the United States.
